raw_response:
I'm sixty-two this year, and I've been farming these 15 mu for forty years. I only went to primary school, but I know this land better than anyone with a diploma. It's just me now — my wife passed five years ago, and my son works in a factory in Shijiazhuang. He sends a little money at Spring Festival, but I have to make do on my own the rest of the year.

I keep 6 mu in wheat and then maize, same as always. That's my food security and some cash. The other 9 mu is stevia I planted two years back. My nephew said the buyer from the county processing plant pays steady, and at my age it's easier on my back than hauling wheat sheaves all day. Still, 9 mu is a lot for one old man, so I hire village women to help with the cutting.

The wheat went in last October, right after I got the maize out. I used the local improved seed — about 12 yuan per mu. I hired Lao Zhang's tractor to till and plant, cost me about 50 yuan per mu but I can't do it alone anymore at my age. I put down base fertilizer then: about 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. Now it's March and the wheat is turning green. I'll give it the "returning green water" soon — pumping from the well costs about 25 yuan per mu each time, but I have to do it. Then at jointing I'll spread about 30 jin of urea per mu. Last year I only did 20 jin to save money, and my yield dropped to 350 jin per mu. That was stupid — I saved 20 yuan on fertilizer and lost 100 yuan in grain. This year I'm doing the full 30 jin, and I'll irrigate twice more if it stays dry: at jointing and at heading. Three irrigations total. I expect about 400 jin per mu, so 2,400 jin from the 6 mu. I'll spray herbicide once in spring, and if I see yellow rust I'll spray fungicide too.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in mid-June. The window is tight — sometimes only five or six days — so I hire the planter. Seed costs about 50 yuan per mu for the hybrid. I put compound fertilizer down with the planter, about 35 jin per mu, then topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage, about 25 jin per mu. Two irrigations: one at big trumpet, one at grain filling. I spray herbicide before emergence and insecticide for corn borer. If the weather is normal I should get 450 jin per mu, about 2,700 jin total.

The stevia is established now. In March I spread compound fertilizer, about 30 jin per mu, and irrigate once. I cut the leaves three times: first in mid-June, second in August, third in October. After the first two cuts I give it some urea water to help it grow back. Two more irrigations in summer if it's dry. I hire two village women to help with each harvest — 4 days per cut, 12 days total — because bending down to cut 9 mu three times would break my old back. Each mu should give about 120 jin of dried leaves, so roughly 1,080 jin total. The buyer comes to the village, which saves me hauling it far on my bike.

I do most of the day-to-day work myself — irrigating, fertilizing, spraying. But for wheat harvest, maize planting, and stevia cutting, I need help. Machinery for wheat harvest is 50 yuan per mu, maize planter is 40 yuan per mu, maize harvest is another 50 yuan per mu. The women get 80 yuan per day.

My total costs this year will run about 5,800 yuan. That's a lot for one old man. I thought about cutting back on fertilizer to save money, but last time I did that I lost more in yield than I saved. Better to spend the money and eat proper. I need to keep a few hundred yuan aside for doctor visits too — at sixty-two, you never know when your back or your heart will act up.
